issue.title: Fix footer Reset falling back to a stale selected-expense currency
issue.body:
<!-- If necessary, assign reviewers that know the area or changes well. Feel free to tag any additional reviewers you see fit. -->

### Explanation of Change

The footer's Reset/default currency fell back to the selected expense's own currency, so after changing Preferences > Payment currency, Reset kept restoring the old currency.

The Reset/default currency now comes from the active policy's output currency (the personal policy's for accounts without a workspace, which is what Preferences > Payment currency edits). This mirrors the currency the server converts search figures to when the query has no explicit target.

Reset also passes that currency through as an explicit selection instead of clearing the choice. The existing default chain compares it against the currency the loaded figures are denominated in, so the conversion machinery runs exactly when the figures are in another currency and stays idle otherwise.

Also changed `SearchResultsProvider`'s `defaultSearchInfo.currency` from `''` to `undefined` so an unset search currency is always `undefined`.

### Fixed Issues
$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97583
PROPOSAL:


### Tests

1. As a fresh account with no workspace, go to a self-DM and create an expense.
2. Go to Spend > Expenses and select the expense via checkbox.
3. Go to Account > Preferences > Payment currency and change it to a currency different from step 1's default (e.g. USD).
4. Go back to Spend > Expenses and select the expense via checkbox.
5. Click the currency selector on the footer, then click Reset.
6. Verify the currency resets to the payment currency chosen in step 3 and the total amount is converted to it.
7. Repeat steps 4-6 after switching to Reports and back to Expenses (the previously-working path) to confirm no regression.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e9a2db3-1e30-45ee-95c0-fc26d2a76911






- [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console

### Offline tests

Not affected — the payment currency is read from already-persisted Onyx data (`PERSONAL_POLICY_ID` and the personal policy), same as before; no new network requests are introduced.

### QA Steps

1. As a fresh account with no workspace, go to a self-DM and create an expense.
2. Go to Spend > Expenses and select the expense via checkbox.
3. Go to Account > Preferences > Payment currency and change it to a different currency.
4. Go back to Spend > Expenses, select the expense, open the footer currency selector, and click Reset.
5. Verify the currency resets to the payment currency chosen in step 3 and the total amount is converted to it.

issue.title: Reuse the saved CSV layout settings when uploading again into an existing card
issue.body:
### Explanation of Change

Uploading a second file into a card that was created from a CSV imports the new transactions with their raw negative amounts, ignoring the flip amount sign choice made on the first upload. The choices made on the first upload's setup screen are held in a temporary store that is cleared once an import finishes, and uploading again into an existing card goes straight to the file picker, so that setup screen never runs a second time. The import therefore falls through to its hardcoded defaults, which do more than skip the sign flip: they also replace the chosen currency with USD, mark the transactions reimbursable, and rename the card. Those defaults are then written back over the card's saved layout, so every later upload inherits them as well.

The card's saved layout already stores all four of these choices, and the import already receives it in order to roll back on failure. Each setting is now resolved from the current selection first, then from that saved layout, then from the existing default. Resolving field by field, and only when a value is absent, means a deliberately disabled setting is preserved instead of being treated as missing. First-time uploads are unaffected, since they have no saved layout and always supply all four settings themselves.

### Fixed Issues

$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97779
PROPOSAL: https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97779#issuecomment-5182742021

### Tests

1. Prepare a CSV of bank transactions where all the transactions have a -ve value. The issue does not include the reporter's files, so the one used below is attached for convenience. The same file is uploaded twice, so the second upload's only difference comes from the settings being reused or lost.

<details>
<summary>Sample CSV file</summary>

[import-first.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wildan-m/App/screenshots-97779/import-first.csv)

```csv
Date,Merchant,Amount
2026-01-15,Coffee Shop,-5.50
2026-01-20,Restaurant,-25.00
```

</details>

2. Go to Account > Wallet > Import transactions.
3. Set up the import with a card display name, a non-USD currency (e.g. EUR), **Transactions are reimbursable** turned off, and **Flip amount sign** turned on.
4. Upload the file, check the mapping and import it. Verify the transactions are positive and in the chosen currency.
5. Go back to Account > Wallet, click into the card you just created, and choose **Import spreadsheet**. Note there is no **Flip amount sign** option on this path.
6. Upload the same file again, check the mapping and upload.
7. Verify the second batch duplicates the first exactly — positive, in the same non-USD currency, and not marked reimbursable — instead of arriving as negative USD amounts marked reimbursable.
8. Reopen the card details and verify the card name is unchanged and **Mark transactions as reimbursable** is still off.

- [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console

### Offline tests

The change only affects which values the import starts from, not how the request is made, so offline behaviour is unchanged. The import still queues optimistic transactions and an optimistic saved layout before the request, and still restores the card's previous saved layout if the request ultimately fails.

Same as tests.

issue.title: Reuse the saved CSV layout settings when uploading again into an existing card
issue.body:
### Explanation of Change

Uploading a second file into a card that was created from a CSV imports the new transactions with their raw negative amounts, ignoring the flip amount sign choice made on the first upload. The choices made on the first upload's setup screen are held in a temporary store that is cleared once an import finishes, and uploading again into an existing card goes straight to the file picker, so that setup screen never runs a second time. The import therefore falls through to its hardcoded defaults, which do more than skip the sign flip: they also replace the chosen currency with USD, mark the transactions reimbursable, and rename the card. Those defaults are then written back over the card's saved layout, so every later upload inherits them as well.

The card's saved layout already stores all four of these choices, and the import already receives it in order to roll back on failure. Each setting is now resolved from the current selection first, then from that saved layout, then from the existing default. Resolving field by field, and only when a value is absent, means a deliberately disabled setting is preserved instead of being treated as missing. First-time uploads are unaffected, since they have no saved layout and always supply all four settings themselves.

### Fixed Issues

$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97779
PROPOSAL: https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97779#issuecomment-5182742021

### Tests

1. Prepare a CSV of bank transactions where all the transactions have a -ve value. The issue does not include the reporter's files, so the one used below is attached for convenience. The same file is uploaded twice, so the second upload's only difference comes from the settings being reused or lost.

<details>
<summary>Sample CSV file</summary>

[import-first.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wildan-m/App/screenshots-97779/import-first.csv)

```csv
Date,Merchant,Amount
2026-01-15,Coffee Shop,-5.50
2026-01-20,Restaurant,-25.00
```

</details>

2. Go to Account > Wallet > Import transactions.
3. Set up the import with a card display name, a non-USD currency (e.g. EUR), **Transactions are reimbursable** turned off, and **Flip amount sign** turned on.
4. Upload the file, check the mapping and import it. Verify the transactions are positive and in the chosen currency.
5. Go back to Account > Wallet, click into the card you just created, and choose **Import spreadsheet**. Note there is no **Flip amount sign** option on this path.
6. Upload the same file again, check the mapping and upload.
7. Verify the second batch duplicates the first exactly — positive, in the same non-USD currency, and not marked reimbursable — instead of arriving as negative USD amounts marked reimbursable.
8. Reopen the card details and verify the card name is unchanged and **Mark transactions as reimbursable** is still off.

- [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console

### Offline tests

The change only affects which values the import starts from, not how the request is made, so offline behaviour is unchanged. The import still queues optimistic transactions and an optimistic saved layout before the request, and still restores the card's previous saved layout if the request ultimately fails.

issue.title: Reuse the saved CSV layout settings when uploading again into an existing card
issue.body:
### Explanation of Change

Uploading a second file into a card that was created from a CSV imports the new transactions with their raw negative amounts, ignoring the flip amount sign choice made on the first upload. The choices made on the first upload's setup screen are held in a temporary store that is cleared once an import finishes, and uploading again into an existing card goes straight to the file picker, so that setup screen never runs a second time. The import therefore falls through to its hardcoded defaults, which do more than skip the sign flip: they also replace the chosen currency with USD, mark the transactions reimbursable, and rename the card. Those defaults are then written back over the card's saved layout, so every later upload inherits them as well.

The card's saved layout already stores all four of these choices, and the import already receives it in order to roll back on failure. Each setting is now resolved from the current selection first, then from that saved layout, then from the existing default. Resolving field by field, and only when a value is absent, means a deliberately disabled setting is preserved instead of being treated as missing. First-time uploads are unaffected, since they have no saved layout and always supply all four settings themselves.

### Fixed Issues

$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97779
PROPOSAL: https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97779#issuecomment-5182742021

### Tests

1. Prepare a CSV of bank transactions where all the transactions have a -ve value. The issue does not include the reporter's files, so the one used below is attached for convenience. The same file is uploaded twice, so the second upload's only difference comes from the settings being reused or lost.

<details>
<summary>Sample CSV file</summary>

[import-first.csv](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wildan-m/App/screenshots-97779/import-first.csv)

```csv
Date,Merchant,Amount
2026-01-15,Coffee Shop,-5.50
2026-01-20,Restaurant,-25.00
```

</details>

2. Go to Account > Wallet > Import transactions.
3. Set up the import with a card display name, a non-USD currency (e.g. EUR), **Transactions are reimbursable** turned off, and **Flip amount sign** turned on.
4. Upload the file, check the mapping and import it. Verify the transactions are positive and in the chosen currency.
5. Go back to Account > Wallet, click into the card you just created, and choose **Import spreadsheet**. Note there is no **Flip amount sign** option on this path.
6. Upload the same file again, check the mapping and upload.
7. Verify the second batch duplicates the first exactly — positive, in the same non-USD currency, and not marked reimbursable — instead of arriving as negative USD amounts marked reimbursable.
8. Reopen the card details and verify the card name is unchanged and **Mark transactions as reimbursable** is still off.

- [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console

### Offline tests

The change only affects which values the import starts from, not how the request is made, so offline behaviour is unchanged. The import still queues optimistic transactions and an optimistic saved layout before the request, and still restores the card's previous saved layout if the request ultimately fails.

issue.title: Reuse the saved CSV layout settings when uploading again into an existing card
issue.body:
### Explanation of Change

Uploading a second file into a card that was created from a CSV imports the new transactions with their raw negative amounts, ignoring the flip amount sign choice made on the first upload. The choices made on the first upload's setup screen are held in a temporary store that is cleared once an import finishes, and uploading again into an existing card goes straight to the file picker, so that setup screen never runs a second time. issue.body:
To make the app easier to navigate we want to add navigation suggestions to the Search router. At a high level it allows users to type `Spend` to go to the `Spend` page. Here's a quick demo of how it works: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/80b27ffe-d1f2-4ce8-912a-1822c8475d40 In addition to the navigation items we're also adding the create menu (floating action button menu) which allows them to quickly create expenses, reports, etc. > [!NOTE] > I also made a [prototype PR](https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/92179) if you want to see how this works in action. The source of truth should be the below as some of the indexing isn't fully covered in my PR. ## What we index | Area | Item | | ---- | ---- | | Top level | `Home`, `Spend`, `Inbox`, `Workspaces`, `Account` | | Spend | Everything in the left hand nav | | Workspaces | Everything in the workspace menu. `Overview`, `Members`, `Rooms`, `Workflows` etc | | Account | Everything in the account menu except for `What's new`, `Sign out`, `Save the world` | | Create menu | Everything in the menu except the quick action | Few things of note: - As you can see above it's mostly about exclusions so it'd be great for scalability if we can include everything in these sections by default and remove the ones that doesn't make sense - The user should only see what they have access to - This should not change **anything** about the current search functionality - Let's also ensure that all these items don't show up until the user has entered a query longer than 2 characters to ensure this doesn't happen: ## UI changes 1. Everything in the table above that isn't `Create menu`, gets `Go to [page/screen title]`. The create items is labeled as they are in the menu. 2. For high-level or create menu there's no icons on the right. For Spend and Account we have an icon + the tab title. For everything in workspace we add the workspace name and the avatar. 3. The specs of the added UI: cc @Expensify/design @trjExpensify

issue.body:
## Problem When a report is marked as paid ("paid elsewhere" / manual reimbursement) in NewDot, admins have no way to reverse that to edit the report. There is currently a gap: once a report is marked as paid, it's effectively locked, even though no real money moved. In Classic, admins can Unapprove a manually-paid report, which reverts it all the way to Outstanding (returning to the last approver). ## Proposed solution Add a **Cancel payment** action for manually-paid reports in NewDot, giving admins a cleaner recovery path: - **Cancel payment** on a marked-as-paid report → returns the report to its pre-payment state so the admin can re-pay or change approver without redoing the approval chain. The exact state depends on the workspace's approval workflow: - It'll go back to **Approved** if approvals are enabled on the workflow - It'll go back to **Done** if approvals are not enabled - From there, **Unapprove** → **Outstanding** to make edits, or **Change approver** to reapprove / re-mark as paid as necessary. Surfacing Cancel payment (rather than only Unapprove-straight-to-Outstanding) gives admins finer control, since returning to Approved/Processing/Done is a less destructive intermediate state than jumping straight to Outstanding. ## Why this is NewDot-only / low risk - The action gating for NewDot is decided client-side in App (`src/libs/ReportSecondaryActionUtils.ts` — `isCancelPaymentAction` / `isUnapproveAction`). Classic computes its own action availability separately, so a NewDot-only client change does not affect Classic behavior. - The backend already supports reverting a manual ("elsewhere") payment back to its pre-payment state without moving any money — no new backend logic is required for the core flow. ## Scope / things to nail down 1. Confirm and, if needed, repair the `isCancelPaymentAction` gating so **Cancel payment** reliably surfaces on manually-paid reports for the admin/payer. (At current HEAD this predicate appears to already return `true` for a manually-paid report when the user is admin+payer — so the production gap may be a bug in the predicate rather than a missing feature. Worth confirming a repro first.) 2. Account for approval-workflow / policy-mode variations in the resulting state after cancel: - Standard submit-and-approve (and non-optional instant-submit): → **Approved** (the common case) - Multi-level / advanced approval workflows: → **Processing** or **Done** depending on where the report sits in the chain - Optional-approval workspace: → Approved state but **Closed** status - Instant-submit + optional-approval: → **Outstanding** (Submitted) Make sure the UX/copy handles the cases where the report does not land on Approved. 3. No changes to Classic or shared backend gating probes. _Reported in [Slack](https://expensify.slack.com/archives/C049HHMV9SM/p1782226869734079)._

issue.title: Filter DELETE-pending transactions out of LHN RBR aggregation
issue.body:
### Explanation of Change

Reverting a split on a report removes the split child transaction(s) optimistically — they are marked with `pendingAction: DELETE` and stay in Onyx (with their `reportID` and their `transactionViolations` entry) until the server confirms and nulls them.

The LHN red-dot (RBR) is computed by `getViolatingReportIDForRBRInLHN` in `src/libs/ReportUtils.ts`. It built the report's transaction set with a plain `getReportTransactions(...)` and did **not** exclude transactions that are pending deletion. That set is passed down into `hasVisibleViolationsForUser` / `hasViolations` / `hasWarningTypeViolations` / `hasNoticeTypeViolationsForRBRInLHN`, each of which reads `transactionViolations_<transactionID>` for every transaction — so a `DELETE`-pending transaction whose violation entry still existed kept the red dot lit.

Meanwhile the report contents (and the sibling "is this report empty" check a few lines above in the same file) already filter out `DELETE`-pending transactions, which is why the opened report looked clean. The LHN aggregation and the report view disagreed about whether the reverted transaction still existed.

This PR makes the RBR aggregation ignore transactions that are already pending deletion, mirroring the empty-report check in the same function:

```ts
const transactions = getReportTransactions(potentialReport.reportID).filter((transaction) => transaction.pendingAction !== CONST.RED_BRICK_ROAD_PENDING_ACTION.DELETE);
```

Because this filtered array is the one handed to every downstream violation check, the single change fixes the whole RBR path in one place and keeps the LHN consistent with what the opened report actually renders — for reverted splits and any other flow that leaves a transaction queued for deletion.

A unit test was added to `tests/unit/ReportUtilsTest.ts` covering the case where the only violating transaction is `DELETE`-pending, asserting `getViolatingReportIDForRBRInLHN` returns `null`.

### Fixed Issues

$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/96967
PROPOSAL: https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/96967#issuecomment-5070690516

### Tests

1. Open a report and move some expenses onto it.
2. Split an expense on the report.
3. Revert the split.
4. Open the report and observe there are no per-transaction violations to fix.
5. Verify the report's RBR (red-dot) indicator in the LHN is **not** shown while the reverted split's child transaction is still queued for deletion.
6. Verify reports that genuinely have violations still show the RBR indicator.

- [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console

### Offline tests

1. Go offline.
2. Split an expense on a report, then revert the split.
3. Verify the LHN does not show a policy-violation red-dot for that report while the reverted child transaction sits pending deletion.
4. Go back online and verify the state stays consistent after the server confirms the removal.

### QA Steps

2. Split an expense on the report.
3. Revert the split.
4. Open the report and confirm there are no per-transaction violations to fix.
5. Verify the report no longer shows a policy-violation red-dot (RBR) indicator in the LHN.
6. Verify reports that do have real violations still display the RBR indicator.

issue.title: Concierge optimistic reveal: switch to a flat cadence

labels.name: Reviewing
labels.description: Has a PR in review

labels.name: Weekly
labels.description: KSv2

issue.body:
## Problem

Concierge's optimistic reply reveal ("trickle") feels noticeably slow compared to ChatGPT and Claude. It's driven by an ease-out curve over a fixed total duration, which produces a variable rate (~13–19 chars/sec at the start decaying to ~7 chars/sec at the end, ~6.7 avg) rather than a steady typing feel.

## Updated plan (flat cadence, optimistic path only)

Present the optimistic response at a **flat, constant cadence** — drop the ease-out curve and the fixed-total-duration knob from the optimistic reveal so it reveals at a steady rate regardless of length. Once server streaming speed improves, the "balanced timing" that these knobs provided is no longer needed.

**Important constraint — do not touch the server-response trickle.** `DEFAULT_STREAM_DURATION_MS` and `easeOut` are *not* optimistic-only. They are also consumed by the server-streamed reveal in [`src/pages/inbox/usePusherDraftPacing.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/ebff9efdf12dc85c964f8eff2c25a9e73ea356a8/src/pages/inbox/usePusherDraftPacing.ts#L394-L395) (via `getRevealDurationMS` + `easeOut`, and `TICK_INTERVAL_MS` for its tick). So they **cannot be deleted outright** without changing server-response behavior. The plan scopes the flat-cadence change to the optimistic path only and leaves the shared constants and the server path exactly as they are on `main`.

## Changes

1. **Revert the earlier shared-constant tweak.** `DEFAULT_STREAM_DURATION_MS` (15,000) and `TICK_INTERVAL_MS` (80) go back to their `main` values. The first version of this work lowered these two constants, but because the server path reads them too, that also made server-streamed replies abrupt (the behavior Shawn flagged). Reverting them fully restores server-response pacing.
2. **Flat cadence for the optimistic path** in [`src/hooks/usePendingConciergeResponse.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/0d1380d36294d8cded4b38c179a22a92f76da81d/src/hooks/usePendingConciergeResponse.ts): the optimistic reveal no longer uses `DEFAULT_STREAM_DURATION_MS` or `easeOut`. It now reveals at a constant rate via a new dedicated constant `OPTIMISTIC_FLAT_MS_PER_TOKEN` (~30 chars/sec), with linear progress instead of ease-out. Total duration scales linearly with length, so every reply reveals at the same steady rate.
3. `easeOut`, `DEFAULT_STREAM_DURATION_MS`, and `getRevealDurationMS` remain in [`ConciergeRevealUtils.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/0d1380d36294d8cded4b38c179a22a92f76da81d/src/libs/ConciergeRevealUtils.ts) because the server path still uses them.

## Open question (follow-up)

Shawn noted the abruptness may partly come from the server sending a complete message mid-reveal, which trips the 1.5s `ACCELERATED_REMAINING_MS` hard limit (the accelerator compresses the remaining optimistic reveal into 1.5s when the canonical reply lands). That's a separate knob from the cadence and is left unchanged here — worth deciding whether to tune it once the flat cadence is validated.

**Slack thread:** https://expensify.slack.com/archives/C090U774ZH7/p1784303172343289

issue.body:
<!-- If necessary, assign reviewers that know the area or changes well. Feel free to tag any additional reviewers you see fit. -->

### Explanation of Change
<!-- Explain what your change does and how it addresses the linked issue -->
This PR preserves the “all matching items” selection when individual expenses are unchecked.

It:

- Tracks unchecked expenses as explicit exclusions while keeping all-matching selection active.
- Automatically selects newly loaded matching expenses while preserving exclusions.
- Shows the total matching count minus excluded expenses.
- Keeps the count and selection stable while loading additional pages or opening and closing expenses.
- Calculates totals on demand without advancing pagination or recalculating totals for every page.
- Passes excluded transaction IDs to supported basic/current-view CSV exports.

1. Please postfix `$` with a URL link to the GitHub issue this Pull Request is fixing. For example, `$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/<issueID>`.

Do NOT add the special GH keywords like `fixed` etc, we have our own process of managing the flow.
It MUST be an entire link to the github issue and your comment proposal ; otherwise, the linking and its automation will not work as expected.

Make sure this section looks similar to this (you can link multiple issues using the same formatting, just add a new line):

$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/<issueID>
$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/<issueID(comment)>

Do NOT only link the issue number like this: $ #<issueID>
--->
$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/94143
PROPOSAL: https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/94143#issuecomment-4782977108


<!--- 
If you want to trigger adhoc build of hybrid app from specific Mobile-Expensify PR please link it like this:

### Tests
<!---
Add a numbered list of manual tests you performed that validates your changes work on all platforms, and that there are no regressions present.
Add any additional test steps if test steps are unique to a particular platform.
Manual test steps should be written so that your reviewer can repeat and verify one or more expected outcomes in the development environment.

For example:
1. Click on the text input to bring it into focus
2. Upload an image via copy paste
3. Verify a modal appears displaying a preview of that image
--->

Precondition: Use an account with more than 50 expenses.

1. Select all matching expenses and Exclude one expense
   1. Navigate to Spend > Expenses.
   2. Open the bulk-selection menu and choose Select all.
   3. Verify the button displays “All matching items selected”.
   4. After selecting all matching expenses, uncheck one expense.
   5. Verify only that expense becomes unchecked.
   6. Verify the button displays the total matching count minus one.
   7. Verify all other matching expenses remain selected.

2. Preserve selection during pagination
   1. Exclude one expense after selecting all matching expenses.
   2. Scroll to the bottom and load the next page.
   3. Verify newly loaded expenses are automatically checked.
   4. Verify the excluded expense remains unchecked.
   5. Verify the selected count does not increase when the next page loads.

3. Avoid recalculating totals during pagination
   1. Select all matching expenses and wait for the total to load.
   2. Scroll to load another page.
   3. Verify the pagination Search request uses `shouldCalculateTotals: false`.
   4. Verify the request loads only the next page.

4. Recheck an excluded expense
   1. Select all matching expenses.
   2. Uncheck one expense.
   3. Recheck the same expense.
   4. Verify it is selected again.
   5. Verify the button returns to “All matching items selected” when no exclusions remain.

5. Exclude multiple expenses
   1. Select all matching expenses.
   2. Uncheck multiple expenses across loaded pages.
   3. Verify every unchecked expense remains excluded.
   4. Verify the selected count decreases once for each excluded expense.
   5. Recheck the expenses and verify the count increases correctly.

6. Verify grouped and expense-report selection
   1. Open a grouped expense or expense-report search.
   2. Select all matching items.
   3. Exclude one selection unit.
   4. Verify the excluded row is displayed as unchecked.
   5. Verify the parent group/report is not displayed as fully selected when one of its expenses is excluded.
   6. Verify newly loaded matching rows remain selected.

7. Verify the selection footer
    1. Select all matching expenses and wait for the count and total.
    2. Exclude one expense.
    3. Verify the footer count subtracts the excluded expense.
    4. Verify the footer total subtracts the excluded expense amount.
    5. Recheck the expense and verify its count and amount are restored.


- [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console

### Offline tests
<!---
Add any relevant steps that validate your changes work as expected in a variety of network states e.g. "offline", "spotty connection", "slow internet", etc. Manual test steps should be written so that your reviewer and QA testers can repeat and verify one or more expected outcomes. If you are unsure how the behavior should work ask for advice in the `#expensify-open-source` Slack channel.

issue.title: Fix: return focus and soft keyboard to description input on iOS after canceling discard modal
issue.body:
### Explanation of Change On the expense **Description** step, canceling the "Discard changes?" modal is supposed to return focus (and the soft keyboard) to the description input. On iOS App it didn't — the keyboard never came back. **Root cause:** opening the "Discard changes?" modal resigns the native soft keyboard on iOS — the modal takes over as the active responder and the IME is dismissed — while the description `TextInput` keeps reporting `isFocused() === true` at the JS layer (the field's focus/editable state is toggled natively, but React Native's focus state is preserved). So the actual driver of the missing keyboard is the **native keyboard being resigned**, not the `isFocused()` value itself. The `onCancel` handler in [`IOURequestStepDescription.tsx`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/pages/iou/request/step/IOURequestStepDescription.tsx#L179) called: ```ts focusComposerWithDelay(inputRef.current)(true); ``` Because `isFocused()` still returns `true` after the modal closes, this hits the "already focused" guard in [`focusComposerWithDelay/index.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/libs/focusComposerWithDelay/index.ts#L37-L43): with `forceKeyboardIfAlreadyFocused` left at its default `false`, the helper early-returns and never re-requests the IME (`input.focus()` is skipped too). So the preserved JS focus state is exactly what stops the keyboard from being restored — the call becomes a no-op and the soft keyboard stays down. The fix passes the third argument so the native keyboard is re-requested even when iOS still considers the field focused: ```ts focusComposerWithDelay(inputRef.current)(true, undefined, true); ``` This routes through the existing native re-focus path ([`requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer/index.native.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/libs/focusComposerWithDelay/requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer/index.native.ts#L14-L21) → `KeyboardController.setFocusTo('current')`), which re-shows the IME without a blur/refocus, and leaves web untouched — the web implementation of [`requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/libs/focusComposerWithDelay/requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer/index.ts#L3-L5) is a `NOOP`. So it targets the iOS regression without side effects on other platforms. ### Fixed Issues $ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97604 PROPOSAL: https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97604#issuecomment-5148828487 ### Tests **Verifies the fix (iOS App):** 1. Start creating an expense: choose **Manual**, enter an amount, and continue to the **Description** step. 2. Type any text in the Description input. 3. Press **Back** to trigger the "Discard changes?" modal. 4. Tap **Cancel**. 5. Verify that when the modal closes, focus returns to the Description input **and the soft keyboard is shown again** (previously the keyboard did not return on iOS). **Regression check (all other platforms — web / Android):** 1. Repeat steps 1–4 above. 2. Verify that after Cancel the Description input still contains the typed text, focus is restored, and there are no console errors or crashes (behavior unchanged from before this PR). > Note: this is a soft-keyboard timing behavior and is environment-sensitive. It may not reproduce on a local dev / simulator HybridApp build (dev-mode JS timing, simulator keyboard differences, local native binary). It should be ad-hoc tested on a **release-mode build on a real iOS device** (matching how QA caught it) to confirm the keyboard/focus is restored before merge. - [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console ### Offline tests Same as Tests — this change only affects focus/keyboard behavior and is independent of network state. ### QA Steps Same as Tests. Verify primarily on **iOS: Native** (release build on a real device) that the keyboard/focus returns to the Description input after tapping Cancel on the discard modal, and confirm no regression on the other platforms. - [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console ### PR Author Checklist - [x] I linked the correct issue in the `### Fixed Issues` section above - [x] I wrote clear testing steps that cover the changes made in this PR - On iOS App it didn't — the keyboard never came back. **Root cause:** opening the "Discard changes?" modal resigns the native soft keyboard on iOS — the modal takes over as the active responder and the IME is dismissed — while the description `TextInput` keeps reporting `isFocused() === true` at the JS layer (the field's focus/editable state is toggled natively, but React Native's focus state is preserved). So the actual driver of the missing keyboard is the **native keyboard being resigned**, not the `isFocused()` value itself. The `onCancel` handler in [`IOURequestStepDescription.tsx`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/pages/iou/request/step/IOURequestStepDescription.tsx#L179) called: ```ts focusComposerWithDelay(inputRef.current)(true); ``` Because `isFocused()` still returns `true` after the modal closes, this hits the "already focused" guard in [`focusComposerWithDelay/index.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/libs/focusComposerWithDelay/index.ts#L37-L43): with `forceKeyboardIfAlreadyFocused` left at its default `false`, the helper early-returns and never re-requests the IME (`input.focus()` is skipped too). So the preserved JS focus state is exactly what stops the keyboard from being restored — the call becomes a no-op and the soft keyboard stays down. The fix passes the third argument so the native keyboard is re-requested even when iOS still considers the field focused: ```ts focusComposerWithDelay(inputRef.current)(true, undefined, true); ``` This routes through the existing native re-focus path ([`requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer/index.native.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/libs/focusComposerWithDelay/requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer/index.native.ts#L14-L21) → `KeyboardController.setFocusTo('current')`), which re-shows the IME without a blur/refocus, and leaves web untouched — the web implementation of [`requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/libs/focusComposerWithDelay/requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer/index.ts#L3-L5) is a `NOOP`. So it targets the iOS regression without side effects on other platforms. ### Fixed Issues $ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97604 PROPOSAL: https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97604#issuecomment-5148828487 ### Tests **Verifies the fix (iOS App):** 1. Start creating an expense: choose **Manual**, enter an amount, and continue to the **Description** step. 2. Type any text in the Description input. 3. Press **Back** to trigger the "Discard changes?" modal. 4. Tap **Cancel**. 5. Verify that when the modal closes, focus returns to the Description input **and the soft keyboard is shown again** (previously the keyboard did not return on iOS). **Regression check (all other platforms — web / Android):** 1. Repeat steps 1–4 above. 2. Verify that after Cancel the Description input still contains the typed text, focus is restored, and there are no console errors or crashes (behavior unchanged from before this PR). > Note: this is a soft-keyboard timing behavior and is environment-sensitive. It may not reproduce on a local dev / simulator HybridApp build (dev-mode JS timing, simulator keyboard differences, local native binary). It should be ad-hoc tested on a **release-mode build on a real iOS device** (matching how QA caught it) to confirm the keyboard/focus is restored before merge. - [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console ### Offline tests Same as Tests — this change only affects focus/keyboard behavior and is independent of network state. ### QA Steps Same as Tests. Verify primarily on **iOS: Native** (release build on a real device) that the keyboard/focus returns to the Description input after tapping Cancel on the discard modal, and confirm no regression on the other platforms. - [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console ### PR Author Checklist - [x] I linked the correct issue in the `### Fixed Issues` section above - [x] I wrote clear testing steps that cover the changes made in this PR - <!-- If necessary, assign reviewers that know the area or changes well. Feel free to tag any additional reviewers you see fit. -->

### Explanation of Change
<!-- Explain what your change does and how it addresses the linked issue -->

This part covers the two transaction-message getters:

- **`getMovedTransactionMessage`** and **`getUnreportedTransactionMessage`** in `ReportUtils` 

Follow-up PRs:
- **Part 4:** `getChatListItemReportName` and `getReportPreviewMessageForCopy` (+ migrate `SearchActionHeader`), thread `derivedReportName` through the local-notification chain and `Task.getShareDestination` (+ `DynamicNewTaskPage`), and replace the remaining `deprecatedGetReportName` call sites with `getReportName`. https://github.com/Expensify/App/pull/98047

### Fixed Issues
<!---
1. Please postfix `$` with a URL link to the GitHub issue this Pull Request is fixing. For example, `$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/<issueID>`.
2. Please postfix  `PROPOSAL:` with a URL link to your GitHub comment, which contains the approved proposal (i.e. the proposal that was approved by Expensify).  For example, `PROPOSAL: https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/<issueID>#issuecomment-1369752925`

Do NOT add the special GH keywords like `fixed` etc, we have our own process of managing the flow.
It MUST be an entire link to the github issue and your comment proposal ; otherwise, the linking and its automation will not work as expected.

Make sure this section looks similar to this (you can link multiple issues using the same formatting, just add a new line):

$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/<issueID>
$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/<issueID(comment)>

Do NOT only link the issue number like this: $ #<issueID>
--->
$ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/66427
PROPOSAL:


<!--- 
If you want to trigger adhoc build of hybrid app from specific Mobile-Expensify PR please link it like this:

MOBILE-EXPENSIFY: https://github.com/Expensify/Mobile-Expensify/pull/<PR-number>

--->

### Tests
<!---
Add a numbered list of manual tests you performed that validates your changes work on all platforms, and that there are no regressions present.
Add any additional test steps if test steps are unique to a particular platform.
Manual test steps should be written so that your reviewer can repeat and verify one or more expected outcomes in the development environment.

For example:
1. Click on the text input to bring it into focus
2. Upload an image via copy paste
3. Verify a modal appears displaying a preview of that image
--->
Same as QA

- [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console

### Offline tests
<!---
Add any relevant steps that validate your changes work as expected in a variety of network states e.g. "offline", "spotty connection", "slow internet", etc. Manual test steps should be written so that your reviewer and QA testers can repeat and verify one or more expected outcomes. If you are unsure how the behavior should work ask for advice in the `#expensify-open-source` Slack channel.
--->

Same as QA

### QA Steps
<!---
Add a numbered list of manual tests that can be performed by our QA engineers on the staging environment to validate that your changes work on all platforms, and that there are no regressions present.
Add any additional QA steps if test steps are unique to a particular platform.
Manual test steps should be written so that the QA engineer can repeat and verify one or more expected outcomes in the staging environment.

For example:
1. Click on the text input to bring it into focus
2. Upload an image via copy paste
3. Verify a modal appears displaying a preview of that image

It's acceptable to write "Same as tests" if the QA team is able to run the tests in the above "Tests" section.
--->
// TODO: These must be filled out, or the issue title must include "[No QA]."

**Test 1 — Moved-transaction system message**
1. Open an expense in report A.
2. From the expense header, open the three-dot menu → **Move to report** → move it to report B in a different workspace.
3. Open report B and locate the moved expense's thread.
4. **Verify** the system message display `moved this expense from <report A name>`, and the link opens report A.

**Test 2 — Unreported-transaction system message (`UnreportedTransactionAction`)**
1. Open an expense that sits in a report.
2. Move it out of the report to the self-DM / Unreported.
3. Open the resulting thread.
4. **Verify** the `moved this expense from <report name>` message renders

issue.title: Fix: return focus and soft keyboard to description input on iOS after canceling discard modal
issue.body:
### Explanation of Change On the expense **Description** step, canceling the "Discard changes?" modal is supposed to return focus (and the soft keyboard) to the description input. On iOS App it didn't — the keyboard never came back. **Root cause:** opening the "Discard changes?" modal resigns the native soft keyboard on iOS — the modal takes over as the active responder and the IME is dismissed — while the description `TextInput` keeps reporting `isFocused() === true` at the JS layer (the field's focus/editable state is toggled natively, but React Native's focus state is preserved). So the actual driver of the missing keyboard is the **native keyboard being resigned**, not the `isFocused()` value itself. The `onCancel` handler in [`IOURequestStepDescription.tsx`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/pages/iou/request/step/IOURequestStepDescription.tsx#L179) called: ```ts focusComposerWithDelay(inputRef.current)(true); ``` Because `isFocused()` still returns `true` after the modal closes, this hits the "already focused" guard in [`focusComposerWithDelay/index.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/libs/focusComposerWithDelay/index.ts#L37-L43): with `forceKeyboardIfAlreadyFocused` left at its default `false`, the helper early-returns and never re-requests the IME (`input.focus()` is skipped too). So the preserved JS focus state is exactly what stops the keyboard from being restored — the call becomes a no-op and the soft keyboard stays down. The fix passes the third argument so the native keyboard is re-requested even when iOS still considers the field focused: ```ts focusComposerWithDelay(inputRef.current)(true, undefined, true); ``` This routes through the existing native re-focus path ([`requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer/index.native.ts`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/libs/focusComposerWithDelay/requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer/index.native.ts#L14-L21) → `KeyboardController.setFocusTo('current')`), which re-shows the IME without a blur/refocus, and leaves web untouched — the web implementation of [`requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer`](https://github.com/Expensify/App/blob/e570d231d4c0a5f085c53f2aed21d2fc98a39632/src/libs/focusComposerWithDelay/requestKeyboardForFocusedComposer/index.ts#L3-L5) is a `NOOP`. So it targets the iOS regression without side effects on other platforms. ### Fixed Issues $ https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97604 PROPOSAL: https://github.com/Expensify/App/issues/97604#issuecomment-5148828487 ### Tests **Verifies the fix (iOS App):** 1. Repeat steps 1–4 above. 2. Verify that after Cancel the Description input still contains the typed text, focus is restored, and there are no console errors or crashes (behavior unchanged from before this PR). > Note: this is a soft-keyboard timing behavior and is environment-sensitive. It may not reproduce on a local dev / simulator HybridApp build (dev-mode JS timing, simulator keyboard differences, local native binary). It should be ad-hoc tested on a **release-mode build on a real iOS device** (matching how QA caught it) to confirm the keyboard/focus is restored before merge. - [x] Verify that no errors appear in the JS console ### Offline tests Same as Tests — this change only affects focus/keyboard behavior and is independent of network state. ### QA Steps Same as Tests. Verify primarily on **iOS: Native** (release build on a real device) that the keyboard/focus returns to the Description input after tapping Cancel on the discard modal, and confirm no regression on the other platforms. - issue.title: [HOLD][No QA] Update help docs for Release 1: Company-paid currency conversion fees

labels.name: HelpDot
labels.description: Apply this label if the issue relates to ExpensifyHelp

issue.body:
<!-- If necessary, assign reviewers that know the area or changes well. Feel free to tag any additional reviewers you see fit. -->

### Explanation of Change

Updates four New Expensify help-site articles for **Release 1** of the Global Reimbursement "Company-Paid Conversion Costs" project. This release introduces a **Currency conversion fees** setting (Company pays / Employee pays) that controls who absorbs foreign exchange costs on cross-border reimbursements, and surfaces the amount debited from the business bank account. The docs are updated to match:

issue.body:
(Neil's AI agent) ## Problem Auto-generated government rates appear identical to manually-created rates in the workspace distance rates list, so admins can't tell which rates are managed automatically. ## Solution - Extend the release-1 `DistanceRateTableItem` (Rate column) to render a lightning-bolt `Icon` with a `Tooltip` ("This rate is auto-generated") when a new util `isGovernmentRateUnmodified(rate)` returns true (i.e. `rate.attributes.governmentRate` still matches `rate`, `startDate`, `endDate`). - Rate type update: rename `TaxRateAttributes` -> `RateAttributes`, add a `GovernmentRateSnapshot` type (`sourceRateID`, `rate`, `startDate`, `endDate`) and a `governmentRate` field on `RateAttributes`, and update all imports/usages. issue.title: Filter DELETE-pending transactions out of LHN RBR aggregation
issue.body:
### Explanation of Change

Reverting a split on a report removes the split child transaction(s) optimistically — they are marked with `pendingAction: DELETE` and stay in Onyx (with their `reportID` and their `transactionViolations` entry) until the server confirms and nulls them.

The LHN red-dot (RBR) is computed by `getViolatingReportIDForRBRInLHN` in `src/libs/ReportUtils.ts`. It built the report's transaction set with a plain `getReportTransactions(...)` and did **not** exclude transactions that are pending deletion. That set is passed down into `hasVisibleViolationsForUser` / `hasViolations` / `hasWarningTypeViolations` / `hasNoticeTypeViolationsForRBRInLHN`, each of which reads `transactionViolations_<transactionID>` for every transaction — so a `DELETE`-pending transaction whose violation entry still existed kept the red dot lit.

Meanwhile the report contents (and the sibling "is this report empty" check a few lines above in the same file) already filter out `DELETE`-pending transactions, which is why the opened report looked clean. The LHN aggregation and the report view disagreed about whether the reverted transaction still existed.

This PR makes the RBR aggregation ignore transactions that are already pending deletion, mirroring the empty-report check in the same function:

```ts
const transactions = getReportTransactions(potentialReport.reportID).filter((transaction) => transaction.pendingAction !== CONST.RED_BRICK_ROAD_PENDING_ACTION.DELETE);
```

Because this filtered array is the one handed to every downstream violation check, the single change fixes the whole RBR path in one place and keeps the LHN consistent with what the opened report actually renders — for reverted splits and any other flow that leaves a transaction queued for deletion.

A unit test was added to `tests/unit/ReportUtilsTest.ts` covering the case where the only violating transaction is `DELETE`-pending, asserting `getViolatingReportIDForRBRInLHN` returns `null`.

issue.title: Preserve Search context when deleting tasks
issue.body:
<!-- If necessary, assign reviewers that know the area or changes well. Feel free to tag any additional reviewers you see fit. -->

### Explanation of Change
<!-- Explain what your change does and how it addresses the linked issue -->

When a task is deleted from `Spend > Chats/Search`, the app should return to the same Search-owned route instead of navigating to an Inbox-owned report route. This change uses the task details route’s existing backTo value before deleting the task, so the user stays in the Search context while preserving the existing fallback behavior for non-Search task deletes.

It MUST be an entire link to the github issue and your comment proposal ; otherwise, the linking and its automation will not work as expected.

Do NOT only link the issue number like this: $ #<issueID>
